scope: Read-only original-resolution waist crops, with independent visual review
findings: The longitudinal abdominal depression is more confidently identifiable as the navel region because a local dark hollow is visible in the folded-arms image and its shape recurs in the similar-pose image. Exact center remains approximate.

Real references already show unequal projected left/right distances from the navel: image-right straps are near the outer contour and foreshortened while image-left spans are longer. Do not enforce mirror symmetry or equal pixel distances.

Folded-arms reference exposes the image-right pair near the abdominal edge; similar-pose reference exposes only a short right segment next to the hand. Neither supplies the full right pulled path or hidden attachment in the target pose.

The added evidence favors testing an outward/image-right waistband entry and a steeper right descending span, constrained by the original short strap direction. It does not validate a precise anchor or prove crossing impossible under tension.
status: Useful constraints obtained; no photo edits; exact hidden anchors unresolved
